A.explanation: If $n=1$, the denominator has units $\text{kg m}^{-1} \text{s}^{-1}$, which does not match the newton unit of $F$.

B.explanation: With $n=2$, $v^2 \rho A$ has units $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, same as $F$, so $C_d$ is dimensionless.

C.explanation: If $n=3$, the denominator has units $\text{kg m s}^{-3}$, leaving $C_d$ with units $\text{m}^{-1} \text{s}$.

D.explanation: If $n=4$, the denominator has units $\text{kg m}^2 \text{s}^{-4}$, leaving $C_d$ with units $\text{m}^{-1} \text{s}^{2}$.

hints: Notice that $C_d$ has no units, so the combination $v^n \rho A$ in the denominator must have exactly the same units as the drag force $F$ in the numerator.
Recall the SI units present here: $F$ in $\text{N}$ or $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$, $\rho$ in $\text{kg m}^{-3}$, $A$ in $\text{m}^2$ and $v$ in $\text{m s}^{-1}$.
Write the homogeneity equation $[F] = [v]^n[\rho][A]$ and compare powers of $\text{s}$ first, then check powers of $\text{m}$ to find $n$.
walkthrough: The equation is $C_d = 2F / (v^n \rho A)$ and $C_d$ is dimensionless, so by homogeneity the denominator must have the same base units as $F$.
Write each quantity in base SI units: $[F] = \text{kg m s}^{-2}$, $[v]^n = (\text{m s}^{-1})^n = \text{m}^n \text{s}^{-n}$, $[\rho] = \text{kg m}^{-3}$, $[A] = \text{m}^2$.
Multiply the denominator units: $[v^n \rho A] = \text{m}^n \text{s}^{-n} \times \text{kg m}^{-3} \times \text{m}^2 = \text{kg m}^{n-1} \text{s}^{-n}$.
Check powers of $\text{m}$: $n-1 = 1$ gives $n = 2$, and $\text{kg}$ already matches, confirming homogeneity.
Therefore the denominator has units $\text{kg m s}^{-2}$ like $F$, making $C_d$ unit-free. This is option B.
